description:
This video was made possible thanks to everyone on the Simple History Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/simplehistory

Square bullets weren’t just a concept—they were patented. In 1718, inventor James Puckle developed the Puckle Gun, a revolving flintlock-style design intended to fire faster than traditional flintlocks, using square bullets to try to increase damage on impact. The transcript ties the invention to a defense message and says square bullets were meant to be more likely to go through armor—specifically in the context of the Ottoman Empire. But it also says it didn’t impress the British Navy and never won investors for production. What other early firearm experiments should we cover next?
